lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about one child - my 8-year-old, Alex. I'm in the process of adopting them, but they haven't moved in with me yet. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit in this situation?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex. 

To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand your current situation a bit better.

**Has Alex come to live with you yet, or are they still living elsewhere while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't come to live with me yet. They're still living elsewhere while we go through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Based on the rules for Child Benefit and adoption, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as the child comes to live with you - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the child does need to be living with you to make the claim.

Since Alex hasn't moved in with you yet, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit at this time. Once Alex comes to live with you, you'll be able to claim Child Benefit even if the adoption isn't yet finalized.

Before I provide my final assessment, let me ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I live in the UK. 

But I do want to mention - even though Alex isn't living with me yet, I am contributing financially to their upkeep. I help out with about £30 a week for things they need. Does that make any difference to whether I can claim now?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that additional information. That's an important detail.

To assess whether your financial contributions might qualify you for Child Benefit before Alex moves in, I need to understand a bit more about the current arrangement.

**Is Alex currently living with someone else who is caring for them (such as a foster carer, relative, or friend), and if so, is that person currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living with someone else right now while the adoption goes through, but no - the person they're staying with isn't claiming Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask one more question to fully understand the situation:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while they are living with this other person during the adoption process?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance where they're currently staying.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me carefully assess your situation based on the Child Benefit rules.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex (age 8) hasn't moved in with you yet
- You are contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- The person Alex is currently living with is not claiming Child Benefit
- The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

According to the rules, you'll normally be responsible for a child if either you live with them OR you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them (for food, clothes, pocket money, etc.).

The current Child Benefit rate for one child is £25.60 per week (for the eldest/only child). Since you're contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit amount, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you could potentially qualify for Child Benefit now, even before Alex moves in with you.

However, there may be specific considerations around adoption cases that I should confirm. Let me ask: **Are you working with an adoption agency or local authority for this adoption, and have they provided any guidance about when you can claim Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I'm working with the local authority on the adoption, but they haven't really given me specific guidance about when I can claim Child Benefit. That's why I'm checking now - I wanted to understand if I'm eligible before Alex moves in, given that I'm already supporting them financially.

So based on what you've said about me contributing more than the Child Benefit amount, does that mean I can go ahead and claim now?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, let me give you my assessment:

You are contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate (£25.60 per week for one child). According to the rules, you'll usually be responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money.

Since:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is under 16 (age 8)
- You are contributing more than the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's upkeep
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

You appear to meet the criteria to claim Child Benefit now, even before Alex moves in with you. The rules about adoption specifically state that you can claim as soon as the child comes to live with you, but the broader responsibility rules (paying at least as much as Child Benefit towards their upkeep) would also apply in your situation.

**You should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex now**, given your financial contributions.

conversation.text:
**Assessment Complete: You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Based on my assessment of your situation, you qualify for Child Benefit because you are meeting the responsibility test by contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep - which is more than the Child Benefit amount. You don't need to wait until Alex moves in with you to make your claim.

When you're ready, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. Good luck with the adoption process!
